text:
alisa: hey team, customer reported embeddings endpoint suddenly spiking p95/p99; they see slower responses and some dimension mismatch errors after a recent rollout. cc @jamal for perf, @mike for infra :eyes:
jamal: got it. can you paste sample error and a minimal repro?
alisa: here's the error from their app: "Embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024". They also shared traces where requests to /v1/embeddings hang for ~700ms more than usual at the routing stage.
mike: routing stage? do we have per-request span breakdown for the embeddings route? what panels did they look at?
alisa: they sent a screenshot of the dashboard but it's fuzzy. asked them to share trace id; provided trace id: trace-0a9b3c4d
sophie: I pulled the trace (trace-0a9b3c4d) from honeycomb. timeline shows: client -> api-gw (60ms) -> auth (5ms) -> embeddings-router (560ms) -> backend-pool (20ms) -> model-srv (150ms). embeddings-router is the big chunk.
jamal: embeddings-router does batching/route selection and dim validation. 560ms suggests either excessive batching wait or a slow KV/cache lookup. do we have the router logs for that trace ts?
mike: ops-bot: get-logs embeddings-router trace=trace-0a9b3c4d
ops-bot: Fetching logs from embeddings-router for trace=trace-0a9b3c4d... (attached) :white_check_mark:
alisa: logs show entries: 
```
2024-06-26T14:17:36Z [INFO] incoming request id=req-9a -> route selection policy=latency_pref
2024-06-26T14:17:36Z [INFO] batched 12 requests, wait_time_ms=400
2024-06-26T14:17:36Z [WARN] payload dims inconsistent inside batch, client_id=cust-873
2024-06-26T14:17:36Z [ERROR] validation failed for req req-9a: expected=1536 actual=1024
```
jamal: ah — "batched 12 requests, wait_time_ms=400". That wait_time is high. normal is ~10-50ms. looks like batch-window widened. could be autoscaling backpressure or poll interval misconfig.
sophie: Also note "dims inconsistent inside batch" — a client sent mixed-size inputs in same batch. our runtime currently validates and rejects at per-request level which adds overhead. we should avoid packing different-dim clients together. routing should isolate by dim and model variant.
mike: I checked autoscaler logs around that time — we had a transient pod restart causing capacity dip, increasing batch window to accumulate enough tokens. restarted pod at 14:16:59Z, steady state restored at 14:18:10Z. that matches the 400ms batching.
alisa: customer also hit dimension mismatch errors — likely due to client-side mixing legacy model calls (old model produced 1024) and new model (1536) in same request. they use a single endpoint but switched model versions recently.
jamal: troubleshooting plan: 1) ask customer for exact request payloads for failing calls 2) advise to pin model version per client or include model hint in request metadata to route separately 3) update router to avoid batching across model-dim groups 4) provide temporary mitigation to lower batch window when dim-inconsistency detected
mike: I'll open infra incident to track the pod restart cause (kube events + node metrics). tagging resources: embeddings-router-deploy v2.3.1
sophie: For observability: I propose adding a per-request dimension field to traces and a dashboard panel showing "batch wait time" histogram and "dim-mismatch count" over time. quick query in honeycomb: group_by(batch_wait_ms) and filter(dim_mismatch=true).
alisa: can we draft a short reply to the customer with repro steps and mitigation? they asked for ETA and root cause.
jamal: draft: "Root cause: transient capacity dip caused router pod restart increased batching wait windows which exposed client mixing of different embedding dims (old/new model). Impact: elevated p95/p99 and some validation errors returning dimension mismatch. Mitigation: pin model version or include model hint in requests to avoid mixed-dim batching; we deployed temporary router patch to reduce max batch window to 50ms when dim inconsistency rate > 0.5%. We'll follow up with permanent router change to partition batches by output-dim and model id."
mike: + mention we are investigating the node/pod restart and will share logs. ETA: patch rolled in canary for router in ~2h, full rollout after validation ~6h.
ops-bot: incident created INC-20240626-42, assigned to @mike; priority=P2
alisa: sending that to the customer now. also included ask for raw request bodies and the client SDK version (they may be on an older SDK).
sophie: followup work items for eng: 
- route partition by (model_id, output_dim) at router level
- instrument per-request "output_dim" tag in tracing
- add continuous alert when batch_wait_ms percentile > 200ms for embeddings-route
- make dim-mismatch errors include helpful guidance to pin model
I'll open tickets.
jamal: thanks all. low-risk customer-facing language and quick mitigations are in place. let's regroup after router canary completes. :thumbsup:
